system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Energy shocks, AI pause and financial stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, tightly coupled process where regional kinetic conflicts, energy chokepoint disruptions and a technology-governance crisis interact with global capital markets and monetary policy to create rapid, systemic instability. Energy supply shocks (Middle East attacks and pipeline closures) amplify inflation and bond-market stress just as AI-sector leaders and governments push for slower development and new rules, while pluralising institutions (BRICS, trade realignments) reshape alliances and fault lines.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, coalitions (NATO, BRICS, GCC), global markets (oil, bonds, FX, crypto), major tech firms and AI labs, multinational firms and supply chains (chips, data centres), international institutions and regulatory processes; the flows, feedbacks and institutions that transmit security, economic and informational shocks across borders.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-technical-economic system (the broader Anthropocene-era global human system of politics, markets, technology and ecology)
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security theatres (Middle East, Europe-Ukraine, Indo-Pacific)
Global finance and macroeconomic policy (bond markets, central banks, FX)
Technology and AI governance ecosystem (labs, platforms, regulators)
Energy and commodity supply networks (oil, LNG, global shipping chokepoints)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by Moscow and Western security partners, are engaged in a protracted high-intensity conflict with shifting tactics, frontlines and supply-chain/energy targeting that drive European security dynamics.

variables.name: Gulf maritime and energy disruption
variables.description: Iran-linked Houthi forces, Gulf states (notably Saudi Arabia), and global naval powers are embroiled in escalating strikes and countermeasures that have shut pipelines and threatened the Strait of Hormuz, producing acute global oil and shipping shocks.

variables.name: AI governance and strategic tech race
variables.description: Major technology firms, U.S. policymakers and international regulators are contesting how fast and under what rules advanced AI should be developed and deployed, creating a cross-border rivalry over standards, investment, and existential-risk management.

variables.name: Global bond and interest-rate shock
variables.description: Central banks (led by the U.S. Fed), global investors and major economies are recalibrating policy in response to persistent inflation and surging sovereign yields, producing volatile capital flows, higher borrowing costs and a repricing of risk worldwide.

variables.name: BRICS-led multipolar realignment
variables.description: BRICS countries and a rising cohort of Global South states are expanding financial, trade and institutional alternatives to Western-dominated systems, shifting the balance of multilateral influence and contesting rules of the international order.
